title: Delegation & the 5 Rights: What the LVN Can Assign to a CNA (California Scope)
subtitle: 68 y/o female, post-op day 1 total hip, type 2 diabetes — the LVN must delegate correctly to a CNA, keep nursing tasks, and escalate what exceeds LVN scope to the RN
nursesNote: 0700 - 68 y/o female, skilled-nursing rehab, post-op day 1 after total hip arthroplasty. History of type 2 diabetes. Stable overnight; alert and oriented x4. Plan of care established by the RN and PT: ambulate with walker with assist, hip precautions, scheduled insulin and oral medications, incision/dressing monitoring. The LVN is assigned this client and works with one CDPH-certified CNA this shift. Pending this hour: routine vital signs on the hall's stable clients, morning bathing/ADLs, intake & output and breakfast tray (client has no swallowing difficulty), scheduled insulin and oral meds, reinforcement of hip-precaution teaching, and assessment of a NEW complaint of increased incisional pain. Morning labs show a low hemoglobin/hematocrit; the provider has ordered one unit of packed red blood cells. The LVN practices under the direction of the RN/provider.

patient.name: M. Delgado
patient.admitDate: SNF rehab, post-op day 1 (total hip arthroplasty)

steps.title: Recognize Cues
steps.sub: Which pending tasks fit the CNA's scope
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) pending tasks that are APPROPRIATE for the LVN to delegate to the CDPH-certified CNA.

opts.text: Obtaining routine vital signs on the hall's stable clients
opts.rat: Routine vital signs on stable clients are within the CNA's scope and are appropriate to delegate — a routine, predictable task with a known outcome.

opts.text: Assisting the client with morning bathing and other activities of daily living
opts.rat: Assisting with bathing and ADLs is core CNA work and is appropriate to delegate.

opts.text: Recording intake and output and delivering the breakfast tray to this client, who has no swallowing difficulty
opts.rat: Recording I&O and delivering a tray to a client with no dysphagia are within the CNA's scope and appropriate to delegate.

opts.text: Administering the client's scheduled insulin
opts.rat: Medication administration requires nursing knowledge and is not within the CNA's scope; the LVN gives the insulin.

opts.text: Assessing the client's new increased incisional pain and inspecting the surgical dressing
opts.rat: Evaluating a new symptom and inspecting a surgical incision are nursing data-collection/assessment tasks, not delegated to a CNA.

opts.text: Reinforcing teaching about hip-replacement precautions
opts.rat: Teaching (even reinforcement) requires nursing knowledge and is not delegated to a CNA.

opts.text: Initiating the ordered unit of packed red blood cells
opts.rat: Starting a blood transfusion is outside the CNA's scope — and in California, outside the LVN's scope as well; the RN initiates it.

steps.title: Analyze Cues
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) statements that correctly reflect safe delegation and the California LVN scope of practice.

opts.text: A delegated task must be within the CNA's scope and follow the 5 rights of delegation — right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction/communication, and right supervision — while the LVN retains accountability and supervises
opts.rat: The 5 rights of delegation guide safe assignment; delegation transfers the task, not the accountability, so the LVN supervises and follows up.

opts.text: Administering medications, reinforcing teaching, and assessing a new symptom require nursing knowledge and are NOT delegated to the CNA
opts.rat: Tasks requiring nursing judgment, assessment, teaching, or medication administration stay with the licensed nurse.

opts.text: Initiating a blood transfusion and giving IV push medications are outside the California LVN's scope; the LVN reports to the RN, who initiates and monitors the transfusion
opts.rat: In California, LVNs do not start blood/blood products or give IV push medications; these are escalated to the RN.

opts.text: Any task may be delegated to the CNA as long as the unit is busy
opts.rat: Workload does not expand the CNA's scope; only tasks within their scope and competency are delegated.

opts.text: Once a task is delegated, the LVN is no longer accountable for it
opts.rat: Accountability for appropriate delegation and supervision remains with the LVN; delegation does not transfer accountability.

opts.text: Because the client is stable, the LVN may independently develop and document a new nursing care plan
opts.rat: Developing the nursing care plan and performing the initial assessment are RN functions; the LVN contributes data but does not create the plan independently.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.sub: Rank the LVN's own tasks by urgency
steps.inst: Drag to rank the LVN's retained tasks from HIGHEST priority (1) to LOWEST (5).

opts.text: Assess the new increased incisional pain and inspect the dressing for bleeding, then report findings
opts.rat: A new symptom with a low hemoglobin/hematocrit raises concern for post-op bleeding; assessing and reporting is the safety priority.

opts.text: Report the low hemoglobin/hematocrit and incision findings to the RN so the RN can initiate the ordered blood transfusion
opts.rat: Escalating the low counts and possible bleeding lets the RN begin the ordered transfusion — timely and beyond the LVN's scope to start.

opts.text: Administer the scheduled insulin for the elevated glucose and the other due medications
opts.rat: Time-sensitive but not emergent; medications are given after the acute concern is assessed and escalated.

opts.text: Reinforce the hip-precaution teaching with the client
opts.rat: Important for a safe recovery but lower priority than the clinical concerns and medications.

opts.text: Give the CNA directions for the delegated routine care and supervise
opts.rat: Coordinating the delegated routine care keeps the assignment safe; it can proceed in parallel but ranks after the LVN's direct clinical priorities.

steps.title: Generate Solutions
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) actions that are appropriate and within the LVN's scope.

opts.text: Give the CNA clear directions for the delegated tasks — what to do, when, and what to report back — and remain available to supervise
opts.rat: Clear direction/communication and supervision are two of the 5 rights and keep delegation safe.

opts.text: Personally administer the insulin and due medications and reinforce the hip-precaution teaching
opts.rat: These require nursing knowledge and are correctly kept by the LVN.

opts.text: Report the low hemoglobin/hematocrit and the increased incisional pain to the RN, and have the RN initiate the ordered blood transfusion
opts.rat: Escalating out-of-scope and clinically significant findings to the RN is the correct action.

opts.text: Ask the CNA to give the insulin and reinforce the teaching so the LVN can chart
opts.rat: Medication administration and teaching are not delegated to a CNA, regardless of charting workload.

opts.text: Start the blood transfusion independently to save the RN time
opts.rat: Initiating blood is outside the California LVN's scope; the RN starts and monitors it.

opts.text: Tell the CNA to assess the incision and decide whether it needs attention
opts.rat: Assessing and clinically judging a surgical incision is a nursing task, not delegated to a CNA.

steps.title: Take Action
steps.inst: Drag the actions from FIRST (1) to LAST (5).

opts.text: Assess the client's incisional pain and dressing and check for bleeding
opts.rat: FIRST — directly evaluate the new symptom and possible bleeding; current data is needed before escalating and acting.

opts.text: Report the findings and the low hemoglobin/hematocrit to the RN using SBAR
opts.rat: SECOND — timely escalation lets the RN initiate the ordered transfusion and reassess the plan.

opts.text: Give the CNA clear directions for the delegated routine care so the whole assignment stays safe
opts.rat: THIRD — delegating routine care frees the LVN for nursing tasks while keeping the assignment covered.

opts.text: Administer the due insulin and medications and reinforce hip-precaution teaching
opts.rat: FOURTH — carry out the retained nursing tasks after the acute concern is handled and routine care is delegated.

opts.text: Document the assessment, delegation, medications, and communication, and follow up on the CNA's reported results
opts.rat: LAST — documentation and follow-up on delegated tasks maintain accountability and continuity.

steps.title: Evaluate Outcomes
steps.inst: Later in the shift, classify each finding.

opts.text: The CNA obtained the routine vital signs and reported them to the LVN, and completed the client's ADLs
opts.rat: Appropriate delegation with report-back kept the assignment safe — effective coordination.

opts.text: After the LVN's SBAR report, the RN initiated the blood transfusion and the LVN assists with monitoring within scope
opts.rat: Correct escalation and role division: the RN starts the blood; the LVN supports monitoring within scope.

opts.text: The LVN finds the CNA about to administer the client's insulin
opts.rat: Medication administration is outside the CNA's scope; the LVN must stop this immediately, give the insulin, and re-clarify the delegation.

opts.text: The client's incisional pain is controlled after intervention and the dressing is dry and intact
opts.rat: The acute concern resolved and there is no sign of active bleeding — a good outcome.

opts.text: The CNA reports that the client felt dizzy during ambulation, so the CNA stopped and notified the LVN
opts.rat: The CNA correctly recognized a limit and reported promptly — appropriate delegation and communication in action.

opts.text: The LVN charted the delegated tasks but never checked whether they were actually completed
opts.rat: Failing to follow up is an accountability/supervision lapse; the LVN must verify delegated tasks were done and the results.

opts.text: Teaching was reinforced and the client correctly restates two hip precautions; a follow-up glucose is being rechecked per order
opts.rat: Correct teach-back and ordered follow-up monitoring indicate the retained nursing tasks are working.

opts.text: The client's daughter asks the LVN to explain the overall plan of care; the LVN refers the question to the RN
opts.rat: Referring a plan-of-care explanation to the RN is appropriate handling within scope — neither deterioration nor a clinical change.

reference: Aligned to the NCSBN NCLEX-PN Test Plan client-need category: Coordinated Care (the app's 'Management of Care' grouping), using the NCSBN Clinical Judgment Measurement Model, and targeting a top LVN blueprint gap (Coordinated Care is 18-24% of the NCLEX-PN exam). Scope statements reflect the California LVN scope of practice under the Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT): the California LVN practices under the direction of an RN/NP/physician; delegates only tasks within a CDPH-certified CNA's scope while retaining accountability and supervising; keeps medication administration, teaching, and assessment as nursing tasks; and does NOT perform the initial/independent assessment, develop the nursing care plan, give IV push medications, or initiate blood/blood-product transfusions (these are RN functions). The 5 rights of delegation are right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction/communication, and right supervision. Apply within current BVNPT regulations and facility policy, which can change. Lab and vital-sign values use standard reference ranges and are illustrative for the scenario; exact clinical figures are confirmed on faculty review by Joseph Ongongo, LPT.
